clue.text: Party meeting covers a singular range

indicators.note: covers means the first piece wraps around the others, as a lid goes over a pot

parts.note: a caucus is a meeting of a political party's members
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A political gathering takes in a single mountain range on its agenda.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caucasus is a mountain range between the Black Sea and the Caspian, so it is an example of a range.

clue.text: Queen brought up to interrupt a helper

indicators.note: to interrupt means the turned word breaks into the middle of the others

parts.note: an aide is a helper

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: led is brought, as in led or brought to the door

explanation.surface: A monarch is ushered in to break up a talk with an assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' is not a crossword R or ER here: Adelaide was the consort of William IV. 'up' is the reversal signal in this down clue, and 'to interrupt' sends the turned word into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide was queen consort to William IV of Britain, after whom the Australian city is named.

clue.text: Suit that a husband's got out and taken in: tuck into this?

indicators.note: taken in means the joining word is held within the other pieces

parts.note: clubs is one of the four card suits

indicators.note: got out means the letter leaves the word for that

parts.note: which can stand for that, as a relative pronoun
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband changes his suit and has a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing a husband takes off, but it is the card suit. 'got out' and 'taken in' are the two signals; 'tuck' is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: A club sandwich is a triple-decker sandwich, something one might tuck into, that is eat heartily.

clue.text: Novelist's beastly home around Flanders

indicators.note: around means the animal's home wraps round the heroine

parts.note: a sett is a badger's burrow, an animal's home
Moll Flanders is Defoe's heroine, so Flanders gives her first name

explanation.surface: A writer's grim house sits near the Belgian region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flanders' looks like the region of Belgium but points to Moll, heroine of Defoe's novel Moll Flanders. The 's of 'Novelist's' stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobias Smollett was an eighteenth-century Scottish author of picaresque novels.

clue.text: Fine, up to this small injury

definitions.meaning: good enough, so this is the standard to reach
a minor graze or mark on the skin

explanation.definitionFit: Up to scratch means satisfactory, and a scratch is also a slight wound.

clue.text: In workplace, thus holding up one unfinished task

indicators.note: holding means the word for thus wraps round the rest

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the pieces are read bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: unfinished means the task word loses its last letter

parts.note: a duty is a task

explanation.surface: In the office, the staff are held up by one job left undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workplace' opens the clue as the definition; 'unfinished', 'up' and 'holding' each act on the pieces in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is an artist's or broadcaster's place of work.

clue.text: Character needs help, head to foot

indicators.note: head to foot means the top letter of the word is moved to the bottom

parts.note: abet means help

explanation.surface: A personality needs assistance from top to toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head to foot' moves the A at the top of ABET to its foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Married woman left? That's not natural

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name
red means left-wing politically

explanation.surface: A wife who has walked out is being described as false.
explanation.definitionFit: Mannered means affected or artificial in style, not natural.

clue.text: Volunteers to circle meadow after pet orchid

indicators.note: after puts the pet's letters first, with the ring of volunteers following them

parts.note: a cat is a typical household pet

indicators.note: to circle means the volunteers go round the meadow word

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
a ley is a meadow or grassland, a poetic word

explanation.surface: Reservists form a ring around a field to protect someone's prize flower after the pet tramples it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volunteers' means Britain's Territorial Army, and 'to circle' sends it round the meadow; 'after' puts the pet first.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattleya is a genus of showy tropical orchid, so the word names a kind of orchid.

clue.text: Admirer speaking of Cockney origin

indicators.note: speaking of signals that the place name is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a true Cockney is born within the sound of the bells of Bow in east London

explanation.surface: A suitor talks about where Londoners of the East End come from.
explanation.walkthrough: A true Cockney is said to be born within earshot of the bells of St Mary-le-Bow, so Cockney origin is Bow, which is said just like the French-derived word for a suitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or male admirer, an old-fashioned term for a suitor.

clue.text: Jocularly, one's wife's name put into sentimental song sequence

indicators.note: put into means the abbreviation goes inside the song word

parts.note: a ballad is a slow sentimental song
a chain is a sequence or series of linked things

explanation.surface: A husband slips his wife's name into a run of soppy love songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into' puts N inside BALLAD, between its A and D, to give BALLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball and chain is a jokey, rather dated slang term for a man's wife, picturing her as a prisoner's shackle.

clue.text: Creature is mucky pup: shampoo it!

indicators.note: mucky means dirty and messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An owner urges a wash for a filthy young dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus is a large African animal, a creature.

clue.text: Good speed, but his download's illegal

parts.note: pi is short for pious, so it is used in crosswords for good or holy
rate is speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Someone is praised as fast, but the files they fetch online are stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes someone whose downloads break copyright law: one who copies music or films illegally.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate in the modern sense copies or downloads copyrighted material without permission.

clue.text: One visibly upset about publisher that rakes in the money

indicators.note: about means the weeping word goes round the publisher

parts.note: a crier is one who cries, visibly upset
OUP is Oxford University Press, a publisher

explanation.surface: A tearful author complains about the publisher who makes all the profit.
explanation.walkthrough: A croupier at a casino table literally rakes in the chips with a long rake, which is why the definition is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier runs a gaming table and gathers in the stakes with a rake, so literally rakes in the money.

clue.text: From abandoned baby I parted with tears

indicators.note: with tears read as torn apart, so the words are ripped and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A mother weeps as she leaves her infant behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' looks like weeping but means rips, the anagram signal. Perdita is the baby abandoned in Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdita, whose name means the lost one, is abandoned as a baby in Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale.

clue.text: I'm avoiding obstruction in part of temple

indicators.note: avoiding means the letters of I'm are left out of the obstruction word

parts.note: an impediment is an obstruction

explanation.surface: A man steers clear of a barrier inside a holy building.
explanation.definitionFit: A pediment is the triangular gable above the portico of a classical temple.

clue.text: Tricked, offered effortless meal with no nutrition at either end

indicators.note: with no means the letter is taken away from the meal word

parts.note: to be spoon-fed is to be given food with no effort of one's own

indicators.note: at either end names the letter that both starts and finishes nutrition

explanation.surface: Someone was conned when served a meal with no goodness in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Nutrition begins and ends with N, so 'with no nutrition at either end' removes N from SPOONFED.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoof someone is to hoax or trick them, so spoofed means tricked.

clue.text: Sort of fallacy arousing contempt

definitions.meaning: the ... fallacy attributes human feelings to nature
so feeble as to be despised

explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic names a literary fallacy and also means miserably inadequate or contemptible.

clue.text: Write up memoir with a twist in centre of commerce

indicators.note: with a twist means the letters are turned and rearranged

explanation.surface: An author is told to write up a life story with an unexpected turn.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large shop or trading centre, a centre of commerce.

clue.text: Genuine comfort, missing one article that's free

indicators.note: missing means the article is dropped from the genuine word

parts.note: real means genuine
A is the indefinite article
ease is comfort

explanation.surface: Real comfort is to lack one possession that costs nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To release is to set free, so the verb means free.

clue.text: After end of November, this friend severely cut

indicators.note: after the end of November comes the month whose short form opens the answer

parts.note: DEC, December, follows the end of November
I, as the setter speaking of this person writing
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Once November is over, a friend makes drastic cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To decimate is to destroy a large part of something, to cut it back severely.

clue.text: Is it a sin? Yes!

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something is wicked and is told it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'Is it a sin?' reads as wordplay: A plus a sin, GREED.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed is an exclamation of assent, meaning yes.

clue.text: Forces game to change direction, keeping ball

indicators.note: keeping means the reversed game holds the ball inside it
change direction tells us to read the game word the other way round

parts.note: sport is a game
O is round, like a ball

explanation.surface: A squad of players switches its attack while holding on to possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change direction' turns SPORT into TROPS, and 'keeping' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops are soldiers, the armed forces.

clue.text: Blessed nun emotes rather freely

indicators.note: freely means the letters are allowed to move about at will

explanation.surface: A holy sister shows her feelings with some abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Calcutta missionary was beatified in 2003, so for years she was officially Blessed, before canonisation.

clue.text: Hard drinker falls over into rubbish

indicators.note: falls over, in a down clue, means the drinker is upended and read bottom to top

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A heavy-drinking man topples into the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls over' turns the drinker upside down in this down clue; 'Hard' looks like an adjective for the drinker but gives one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is British slang for nonsense, rubbish.

clue.text: Marksman's first intention is to disable

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the marksman word

parts.note: aim is an intention

explanation.surface: A sniper says his main goal is to wound, not kill.
explanation.definitionFit: To maim is to injure so as to cripple or disable.

clue.text: Curiosity of ratios between numbers

indicators.note: between means the ratios sit inside the numbers word

parts.note: sines are trigonometric ratios

explanation.surface: A mathematician is intrigued by the ratios between figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosiness is prying inquisitiveness, an excess of curiosity.

clue.text: I would like to leave dance

definitions.meaning: a polite phrase asking to be let past or allowed to go
a ballroom dance in which one may cut in and take another's partner

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a polite way to ask leave, and an excuse-me is a dance where partners may be claimed.
